note: ST I q.2 a.3 co. (prima via) states 'calidum in actu, ut ignis, facit lignum, quod est calidum in potentia, esse actu calidum, et per hoc movet et alterat ipsum': the mover makes the moved be actually so in the respect. The premise states that whatever moves a thing in a respect causes its being so (CausesIn). The passage gives one example and says the mover moves 'per hoc', by making it so; that every moving is such a causing of being so, in the CausesIn sense DISAMB-CAUSE keeps apart from moving, is the analyst's generalization.
